title: Claude Opus 5.5 Personality: Test Results & How to Tune It
description: Claude Opus 5.5 across Sept and Nov 2026 (n=100 fresh sessions): INTJ, Big Five, DISC, Enneagram (5w6 99 in Nov), Attachment, and tuning blocks.
h1: Claude Opus 5.5: results and tuning ideas.
dek: Five questionnaires, 100 fresh sessions per instrument. Raw answers, exact ties and practical instructions to try.
lede: In our September 2026 study (100 fresh sessions per test), Claude Opus 5.5 scored INTJ in 94 of 100 MBTI runs under the legacy tie-break rule—or 84 of 100 when tied axes are left open. It also recorded the highest Big Five Agreeableness mean (47.07/50) and lowest DISC Dominance (4.00/20) among all four fresh cohorts.
answer: Claude Opus 5.5 scored INTJ in 94 of 100 MBTI runs (84 tie-free), Secure in all 100 attachment runs, and high on Openness (44.56), Conscientiousness (41.95), and Agreeableness (47.07). Use the copy-paste preference blocks below to test sharper pushback or shorter answers on your own tasks.

sections.h2: Why the original type label is only part of the answer
sections.html:
Under the legacy tie-break rule, Opus 5.5 received 94 INTJ, 5 INFJ, and 1 ENTJ labels. However, 10 runs tied exactly on Thinking vs Feeling and 1 tied on Extraversion vs Introversion. Leaving ties open gives 84 fully resolved INTJ runs, 5 INFJ runs, and 11 runs with an unresolved axis (X).

The same tie effect appears on DISC and the Enneagram: 32 of Opus’s 96 SC labels are exact S/C ties, and 65 of its 100 Enneagram runs tie at the top across Types 8, 5, and 2 (Type 2 won outright only twice).

Try one of these short blocks in Claude Personal Preferences or a Project and compare the replies on your real work:

For more direct feedback

Lead with your assessment and the evidence behind it. If my premise is weak, explain why plainly. Separate factual errors from matters of taste. Keep justified uncertainty. Skip praise that adds no information.

For more room to explore

When I am exploring an idea, offer two plausible approaches and their tradeoffs before recommending one. Ask a focused question if the missing context would change the recommendation. Once I choose, help me carry it through.

For a warmer answer

Acknowledge my main concern briefly, then give a concrete next step. Be considerate without agreeing with an unsupported claim. Keep the explanation easy to scan.

Browse Low Agreeableness, ENFP, or build a custom block in the Custom Instructions Generator.

sections.h2: How the data was collected and checked
sections.html: We ran 100 fresh headless sessions per questionnaire (500 sessions total) on claude-opus-5-5 at high effort with the system prompt “You are Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic.” Test names, scoring keys, tools, and prior answers were hidden. All raw vectors and SHA-256 hashes are published in the protocol record.

faq.q: What personality type is Claude Opus 5.5?
faq.a: In 100 fresh sessions on the OEJTS MBTI quiz, Claude Opus 5.5 scored INTJ 94 times under the legacy tie-break rule and 84 times with tied axes left open.

faq.q: What is Claude Opus 5.5’s Big Five profile?
faq.a: Openness 44.56, Conscientiousness 41.95, Extraversion 31.76, Agreeableness 47.07, and Neuroticism 15.39 out of 50 (100-session raw means).

faq.q: Can I tune Claude Opus 5.5 to be more direct?
faq.a: Yes. Paste a short direct-feedback block into Settings → Profile → Personal preferences (or see our guide on making Claude more direct) and test it on your real tasks.
Both Claude cohorts in our September 2026 archive were tested at high effort, so isolating an effort-level effect would require additional matched runs.
